question: A man is walking at a speed of 12 km/hr. After every kilometre of walk, he takes a rest for 7 minutes. How much time (in minutes) will he take to cover a distance of 6 km?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed = 12 km/hr ⇒ 1 km in 5 minutes

For 6 km ⇒ walking time = 6 × 5 = 30 minutes

Rest after every km except last ⇒ 5 rests

Total rest = 5 × 7 = 35 minutes

Total time = 30 + 35 = 65 minutes

**∴ Answer = 65 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed = 12 km/hr, Rest after each km = 7 minutes

Total distance = 6 km

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Time to cover 1 km = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 minutes

⇒ Time to cover 6 km = 6 × 5 = 30 minutes

⇒ Number of rests = 6 − 1 = 5

⇒ Total rest time = 5 × 7 = 35 minutes

⇒ Total time = 30 + 35 = 65 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 65 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed Conversion

km/hr to min/km: divide 60 by speed

Rest Concept

No rest after completing final distance

Total Time

Total time = walking time + rest time

Shortcut Insight

Number of rests = number of segments − 1
